notes: This quote is almost certainly not original to Jimi Hendrix. Goodreads tags it explicitly as 'misattributed' and cross-references 'william-gladstone.' Wikiquote's Sri Chinmoy article contains the note that 'a similar statement has also become attributed to Jimi Hendrix, though he could have been quoting or paraphrasing Chinmoy, or conceivably Gladstone.' Sri Chinmoy's 'My Rose Petals' (1971) is the earliest confirmed print citation: 'World Peace can be achieved when the Power Of Love replaces the Love Of Power.' William Gladstone is cited in 'The Forbes Book of Business Quotations' (1997) and in 'The National Elementary School Principal' (Vol. 28, 1948) with a very similar phrasing. An even earlier origin attributed to William Ellery Channing (1780–1842) circulates but is unverified. The exact phrasing in this record ('becomes stronger than' rather than 'overcomes') is a further variant. No primary Hendrix source (interview, recording, written statement) has ever been established. Misattribution to Hendrix is well-documented. | Suggested reattribution: Sri Chinmoy (earliest confirmed print, 1971); possibly William Gladstone or William Ellery Channing for an earlier conceptual antecedent

author: Abraham Lincoln
text: The best way to destroy an enemy is to make him a friend.
notes: Quote Investigator (quoteinvestigator.com/2020/05/13/make-friends/) investigated this thoroughly and concluded: 'based on current evidence this anecdote is apocryphal.' The saying has been attributed to Abraham Lincoln (via a post-mortem Civil War anecdote), Holy Roman Emperor Sigismund (d. 1437), and Mark Twain — all attributions appearing long after each figure's death. An 1867 New Orleans newspaper attributed a similar saying to Sigismund; the Lincoln anecdote form emerged by the 1940s. An 1858 Wisconsin newspaper cited the concept in relation to Cardinal Richelieu. An 1885 Vermont newspaper printed a similar line with no attribution. No primary Lincoln source (speech, letter, diary) has ever been found. The attribution to Lincoln is not credible.
